issue.title: CI flake: large publication-queue backlog exceeds 1.0s wall-clock bound
issue.description:
REPRODUCTION: Scheduled master CI run 31870783076 (https://github.com/sase-org/sase/actions/runs/31870783076) for d19d08641246a2b0f9276fded07d93004815d640 failed job test (3.12) (job 94979384829) with exactly one node after 30157 passed / 56 skipped:

  tests/agents_sync/test_commit_publication_queue.py::test_large_backlog_builds_one_inventory_and_publishes_each_hood_once
  AssertionError: assert 1.5754990230000203 < 1.0
  at tests/agents_sync/test_commit_publication_queue.py:249

The same SHA's earlier push CI run 31861402259 had test (3.12) green, so this is load-sensitive rather than a deterministic break on that tip. Functional assertions in the failing node passed: result.error is None, drained == 2000, one integrate call, one inventory build, one publish per hood, 500-key updates, and the acknowledge set. Only the extra wall-clock guard `assert elapsed < 1.0` around `_publish_queued_locked` failed.

WHY IT MATTERS: this is now a required default-branch CI job failure, not only a local contention tally. sase-h8.10.5.3 already recorded this exact node as a 1/3 just test-contention flake (2026-08-08) and routed it to retired umbrella sase-ct / sase-h8. sase-ct's close reason forbids +1 and requires a narrow task.

SCOPE: decide whether `_publish_queued_locked` genuinely got slower on a 2000-item / 4-hood backlog, or whether the 1.0s perf_counter bound is too tight for GitHub Actions / contended hosts. Do not delete the performance contract. Prefer a contention-independent check (call counts already asserted in the test) or a bound calibrated from recorded CI/history, and keep a regression tripwire. Not attributable to stabilization commit 5601920c9 (ancestor; Python 3.12 passed on the same SHA's push run). Not a process-global leak for epic sase-j7.

VERIFY: the node stays green in isolation and under just test-contention, and a loaded CI-shaped run no longer fails only that wall-clock assert.

RELATED: sase-ct (retired umbrella; do not +1), sase-h8.10.5.3 (prior 1/3 contention tally), sase-j0 (separate 3.13 post-pytest cost-gate redness on the same scheduled run).

The provider-disable epic does not touch publication-queue code; this corroborates the same load-sensitive 1.0s wall-clock-bound defect.

payload.entry: IMPLEMENTATION NOTE: Replaced the single-sample elapsed < 1.0 wall-clock assertion in tests/agents_sync/test_commit_publication_queue.py with deterministic operation bounds for the 2,000-request backlog: one queue snapshot, two cleanup passes, one pull, one commit check, one ahead check, one integration, one inventory build, one publish per hood, four 500-key update groups, and one all-request acknowledgment batch. Verified exact node 4 total passes, contention lane 3/3 with no failed nodes, tests/agents_sync 281 passed, and escalated full pytest 30613 passed / 11 skipped. just check still stops at unrelated Symvision private-import lint failures outside this test-only diff.

CLOSEOUT sase-mi.7: large publication backlog contract remains deterministic-operation based in tests/agents_sync/test_commit_publication_queue.py. Verified full agents-sync suite plus commit-finalizer publication coverage (287 passed) and just test-contention on test_large_backlog_builds_one_inventory_and_publishes_each_hood_once passed 3/3 with zero failed nodes; old single-sample wall-clock flake is no longer the gate.

Fixed by epic sase-mi phase 5 (commit 51ac2c683). The brittle single-sample 'assert elapsed < 1.0' around _publish_queued_locked in tests/agents_sync/test_commit_publication_queue.py::test_large_backlog_builds_one_inventory_and_publishes_each_hood_once is replaced with deterministic operation-count bounds, so the tripwire is contention-independent instead of removed. The functional scaling contract is intact and now asserted explicitly: the 2,000-request / 4-hood workload is unchanged, and the test still pins one outbox listing, one integration, one inventory build, one publish per hood, one payload-clean pair, one pull, one commit check, one ahead check, grouped 500-key updates, and one acknowledgement of every request. A real per-request or per-hood regression still trips those counts; a loaded CI host or a contended local lane no longer fails the node on scheduler delay alone. Verified by the landing agent at HEAD daf933aa5: the exact node plus the whole tests/agents_sync suite are green in a 381-test focused batch; phase evidence additionally recorded just test-contention 3/3 with no failed nodes and an escalated full pytest lane (30613 passed / 11 skipped).
